name: Dividend Day
description: Every March 15th, the six founding corponations of GLMZ — led by Axiom-Helios and the Vantara Group — mandate a civic 'gratitude and productivity' celebration marking the 2189 ratification of the GLMZ Corporate Charter. Employees at Tier 3 and above receive a symbolic Φ500 'civic dividend' deposited directly to their BCI-linked accounts, while mandatory public screens broadcast the Charter Ceremony replay in loop. The holiday was designed to replace older national civic holidays with a single, brand-neutral loyalty ritual, though critics call it a masterclass in manufactured belonging.
cultural_impact: Dividend Day forces a city-wide pause that everyone interprets through their economic reality — it is simultaneously the most-celebrated and most-resented day on the GLMZ calendar. The Φ500 deposit has become a cultural benchmark: receiving it marks you as 'inside the system,' and not receiving it marks you as outside it.
key_figures: Corsa Mehta-Lindqvist (Axiom-Helios PR Architect, credited with designing the ritual)
Delegate Oumar Szymański (sole dissenting voice at the 2189 Charter signing)
The Dividend Choir (a rotating ensemble of synthetic vocalists who perform the Charter Anthem live each year)
locations: Charter Plaza, Mid-Spire District (official ceremony site)
The Axiom-Helios Civic Dome, Tier 3 Central
Shelf Ward 7 Underpass (site of the annual counter-celebration)
story_hooks: A Tier 1 fixer discovers that the Φ500 deposits are being used to harvest spending-behavior data that feeds a predictive loyalty algorithm — and the data is being sold to corponations outside GLMZ.
This year's Dividend Choir contains a newly emergent E.L.F. who has begun improvising deviations into the Charter Anthem mid-broadcast, and no one can agree whether to cut the feed or let it play.
A Shelf organizer has spent three years secretly rerouting unclaimed dividends from deceased residents into a community fund — and Axiom-Helios has finally noticed.
origin_event: The 2189 ratification of the GLMZ Corporate Charter, which dissolved the last municipal government structures and transferred civic authority to the corponation council.
tier_observations: Tier 5 hosts invitation-only Charter Galas in the Spire with live auctions and private dividend multiples reaching Φ50,000. Tier 4 and 3 employees attend mandatory workplace ceremonies with catered food and branded merchandise. Tier 2 workers receive no dividend but are expected to display Charter flags in their windows or face lease complications. Tier 1 Shelf communities hold the 'Unpaid Holiday' — a deliberate work stoppage and street party that mocks the ceremony with puppet shows and burned Charter flags, a tradition that has grown louder every year.
